minutes.headline: Parks Commission votes to fund the part-time recreation director's FY27 salary from its revolving account as a one-year trial
minutes.summary: The Parks Commission approved replacing the memorial scoreboard at Marshall Park, elected new officers (Chris Sullivan as chair, Dan Burns as vice chair) as longtime chair Karen Bernard prepares to leave, and voted to fund the part-time recreation director's salary from the department's revolving account for FY27 as a one-year trial aimed at making the position and eventually the town beach self-sustaining through program revenue. The commission also discussed a draft mission statement, ongoing scheduling friction with the school for program space, and the stalled skate park project now awaiting town counsel.

what_happened.line: The Parks Commission voted to fund the part-time recreation director's FY27 salary entirely from the department's revolving account, as a one-year trial toward a self-sustaining position.
The commission elected Chris Sullivan as chair and Dan Burns as vice chair as longtime chair Karen Bernard prepares to step down.
The commission approved a request from LHS baseball boosters to replace the memorial scoreboard at Marshall Park's 90-foot diamond.
The commission declined to create a discounted seasonal field rate for a short-season youth baseball league, keeping the standard fee with hardship scholarships available instead.
The skate park project remains stalled, still awaiting review by town counsel.

why_it_matters: Paying the recreation director's salary out of program revenue rather than the tax-supported budget is a funding-mechanism shift for the position, with a strategic plan and periodic financial reporting required to track whether it works.
The scoreboard vote and field-fee decision affect who uses Marshall Park and on what terms, including families weighing a hardship scholarship application over a standard rental fee.
The change in commission leadership and a still-unresolved skate park review affect who sets Parks policy going forward and when that project can move.
watch_next: Revised mission statement draft and periodic financial reports on the revolving-account trial

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The two records agree closely on the outcomes of all three votes, the one transfer, and most decisions (the youth-league discount denial, the three future meeting dates, and the vendor-fair table plan), and most figure differences are caption garbling of the same underlying numbers. The biggest things a reader should check are: our minutes omit the specific condition attached to the scoreboard motion (brace must match the plaque's size) and omit the entire mission-statement agenda item and its deferral, our minutes record all votes as informal "voice votes" where the official minutes show roll-call votes 4-0-0, and several names (the outgoing chair, a member, and the recreation director) were misheard by the captions.
